7.BORDERLINE OVARIAN TUMORS (BOT)
•Tumors of low malignant potential.
•More in young Pts.
•10 – 15% of all epithelial ovarian neoplasm.
•5-year survival:
-Stage I = 95 – 97%.
-Stage II = 50 – 86%.
•10 years’ survival 70 – 80%.

Risk Factor:

•Same as Epithelial tumors
•No association with BRCA

p53 mutation = invasive neoplasia

KRAs/BRAF = BOT.

•No progression from 1 form to other.
•BOT can be invasive but low Grade.

Histopathology:

→Serous.
→Mucinous.
→Endometrial.
1.Serous:
•Most common 50%.
•Micropapillary.
•Micro invasive.
2.Mucinous:
•46%
•Intestinal
3.Endometrial:
•Bruner.
•Clear.
•Mixed.

Histological features of BOT:

•Stratified epithelium.
•Varying degree of Atypia.
• Ed mitotic activity.
•Lack of stromal invasion (distinguishing feature).

Symptoms:

•Asymptomatic
•Pelvic pain – long duration than invasive.
•Bloating
•Menstrual irregularity.
•Pressure symptoms.
⇨CA – 125:
-Raised in 75% serous and 30% of mucinous tumors.
⇨CA 19 – 9:

Mucinous.

⇨TVS: variation in appearance.
⇨Doppler: differentiate between benign ad malignant intracystic blood flow.

Referral to oncology MDT

Restaging

Recurrence :8 – 73%.

Relapse:

-with invasive implants – 21% over 5 years.
-with non – invasive implants 2%.

DNA aneuploidy 19-fold in invasive implants.

-12 – 58% after cystectomy.
-0 – 20% after USO/BSO.
-2.5 – 5.7% after completion surgery.

Restaging depends upon:

-Aneuploidy status – DNA.
-Micro papillary status.
-Invasive implants.
-No fertility concerns.
-Fertility in BOT:

Conservative Treatment.

-Spontaneous conception: 32 – 65%.
-OI: 13 – 29%.
-OI only in stage 1 disease for limited cycles.

OI = ovulation
